claims.text: Integrating multiscale descriptors of the HfNbTiVAl10 hierarchical heterostructure into a data-driven model will predict Young’s modulus, yield strength, and fracture behavior more accurately than established simulation methods.
The proposed data-driven model will make these predictions faster than established simulation methods.
The HfNbTiVAl10 alloy is fabricated by arc melting followed by homogenization annealing.
Arc melting and homogenization annealing produce the reported hierarchical heterostructure in HfNbTiVAl10.
Electron microscopy or EBSD images can provide grain-size distributions, phase morphology, and heterogeneity-scale descriptors for the model.
The hierarchical heterostructure contains multiscale variations in grain size and phase distribution.
The hierarchical heterostructure influences load transfer during deformation.
The hierarchical heterostructure influences crack propagation during deformation.
Heterostructural features determine local stress distributions.
Heterostructural features promote or determine crack-deflection mechanisms.
Capturing heterostructural parameters allows a machine-learning model to correlate microstructural state with macroscopic mechanical responses.
The proposed model could reduce prediction error metrics by 20–30% relative to conventional simulations.
The proposed model could reduce processing time by at least 5–10 times relative to conventional simulations.
Inadequate descriptors may cause predictive accuracy to deteriorate at high strain rates or elevated temperatures.
Unresolvable inhomogeneities may cause predictive accuracy to deteriorate.
Model performance may vary with the quality and resolution of the microstructural data.
The model is predeclared as falsified if its predictions deviate by more than 30% from independent experimental values or its efficiency gain is less than fivefold.
